current_affairs.title: India Signs 10-Year Long-Term Bilateral Agreement for Chabahar Port Operation
current_affairs.summary: India Ports Global Limited (IPGL) signed a historic 10-year contract with Iran's Ports and Maritime Organisation (PMO) to equip and operate the Shahid Beheshti Terminal at Chabahar Port.
key_takeaways: Establishes a long-term framework for India's presence at the strategic port in the Gulf of Oman.
Facilitates trade with Afghanistan and Central Asian Republics, bypassing Pakistan.
Acts as a key hub for the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).
current_affairs.mains_relevance: Strategic importance of Chabahar in India's Extended Neighborhood Policy and counter-balancing Gwadar port.

current_affairs.title: G5 Geomagnetic Storm Triggers Rare Auroral Displays at Ladakh Observatory
current_affairs.summary: The Indian Astronomical Observatory (IAO) in Hanle, Ladakh, captured intense auroral activity resulting from an extreme G5 geomagnetic storm caused by strong Solar Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs).
key_takeaways: First time such intense intense stable auroral red (SAR) arcs were recorded in India at low geomagnetic latitudes.
Geomagnetic storms are major disturbances in Earth's magnetosphere caused by solar wind energy exchange.
Poses potential risks to low-Earth orbit satellites, power grids, and GPS navigation systems.
current_affairs.mains_relevance: Understanding solar weather phenomena, space-based observational infrastructure, and threats to critical technological infrastructure.

current_affairs.title: Supreme Court Rules on Custody Powers Under Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA)
current_affairs.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that Enforcement Directorate (ED) officers cannot arrest an accused under Section 19 of the PMLA once the Special Court has taken cognizance of the complaint.
key_takeaways: If an accused appears in response to a court summons, they cannot be deemed to be in custody.
The ED must apply to the Special Court if custody is required post-cognizance.
Reinforces the protection of personal liberty under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
current_affairs.mains_relevance: Balance between executive power, statutory anti-money laundering frameworks, and fundamental constitutional protections.

current_affairs.title: SC-Appointed Panel Evaluates Power Line Undergrounding for Great Indian Bustard
current_affairs.summary: An expert committee appointed by the Supreme Court of India is assessing the technical feasibility of undergrounding overhead power transmission lines in Rajasthan and Gujarat to save the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard (GIB).
key_takeaways: Great Indian Bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps) is listed as 'Critically Endangered' on the IUCN Red List and in Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
Collision with high-voltage power lines is the primary threat to the surviving wild population.
The court highlighted the need to balance renewable energy deployment (solar/wind) with wildlife conservation.
current_affairs.mains_relevance: Environment vs. Development dilemma, conservation strategies for critically endangered fauna, and climate policy integration.

current_affairs.title: Outbreak of West Nile Virus Reported in Kerala
current_affairs.gs_paper: GS Paper III (Issues Related to Health)
current_affairs.summary: The Kerala state health department issued a heightened alert following confirmed cases and vector activity related to the West Nile Virus (WNV) across multiple districts.
key_takeaways: West Nile Virus is a single-stranded RNA mosquito-borne flavivirus.
Maintained in nature through a transmission cycle between birds and Culex mosquitoes.
Humans are dead-end hosts; most infections are asymptomatic, but severe cases cause neuroinvasive diseases like encephalitis or meningitis.
current_affairs.mains_relevance: Vector-borne disease management, public health preparedness, and the role of 'One Health' approaches in controlling zoonotic outbreaks.
